valuation_philosophy: Solution Dynamics is a net-cash NZX micro-cap whose earnings base has RESET, not dipped: the aggregator-reported FY2026 year (revenue ~NZ$31.4m, NPAT ~NZ$0.38m -- unverified, see data_provenance) confirms that the loss of the largest international customer in mid-FY2025 took the business from ~NZ$41m/~NZ$2.6m NPAT to ~NZ$31m/break-even for a full year, with H2 FY2026 revenue (~NZ$14.3m) below H1 (NZ$17.1m). The June 2026 model treated FY2026 as a restructuring trough that would normalize back to ~NZ$2.0m FCF; that is no longer defensible, so this rebuild constructs normalized owner FCF bottom-up from components on the ~NZ$31m base: an IFRS-16 EBITDA margin recovering from ~4% to 9% as cost-out completes, less the ~NZ$0.83m/yr lease cash cost, non-ROU D&A, 28% tax and light capex. That yields a base-case owner FCF ramping from ~NZ$0.56m in FY2027 to ~NZ$1.23m by FY2031 -- roughly the FCF the business earned at NZ$20-23m of revenue in FY2017-18, and well below the pre-reset 9-year owner-FCF median of ~NZ$1.95m. Net cash is the other half of the value and it is being drawn down: an estimated ~NZ$7.17m (~NZ$0.50/share) after the H2 FY2026 cash walk, the buyback and the 4.0c dividend going ex on 10 Sep 2026, versus NZ$8.355m (NZ$0.569/share) in the June model. At NZ$0.625 the market pays ~NZ$0.13/share for the operating business -- about 3x the base-case FY2027 owner FCF -- so this remains a deep-value, asset-backed situation rather than a growth story. Survival, concentration, illiquidity and leadership risk are carried in a 17.5% WACC; the scenarios carry only the operating trajectory. The bear case is a slow cash burn in which the terminal value floors at zero and the asset backing degrades -- the real downside, and one now partly evidenced by negative H1 FY2026 FCF.

historical_cagr.note: CAGRs on FY annual data through FY2025, the last parsed full year. FY2026 (unparsed, aggregator-sourced) is excluded because it is a structural step-down, not a continuation of trend. FCF CAGRs are now on the OWNER-FCF series (reported FCF less lease principal, lease interest and interest income), not reported FCF. None of these rates is used to project the post-reset base case, which is built bottom-up.
historical_cagr.comment: The June model's '9-year median ~NZ$2.8m' was on reported (IFRS-16-flattered) FCF; on an owner basis the pre-reset median is ~NZ$1.95m and the FY2020-25 owner-FCF CAGR is -6.9% -- the business was not compounding cash even before the customer loss. Equity compounded ~18%/yr only because cash accumulated. H1 FY2026 owner FCF was NZ$-2.60m (one-off inserter capex ~NZ$1.3m plus a NZ$1.4m working-capital unwind).
historical_cagr.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (18.3%) diverges >30% from revenue (4.0%) and EPS (7.0%) CAGRs -- driven by cash retention, and all three describe the pre-reset business.

wacc_rationale.currency_basis: NZD flows discounted at an NZD-built rate: NZ 10-yr government ~4.5% risk-free, ~5.5% ERP, small-cap beta/size loading to ~11.5% before company-specific premiums.
wacc_rationale.explanation: Starts from a ~11.5% NZ small-cap WACC and adds explicit structural premiums: +2.0% for severe customer concentration (the largest customer's departure has now cost a full year of earnings and the top-5 remain a large share of revenue); +2.0% for micro-cap illiquidity (market cap ~NZ$9m, thin NZX trading, ~11% held by the Chair); +1.0% for accelerating physical-mail decline (NZ Post postage +26% Jul-2025 on +15% the prior year); +1.0% for management transition -- RAISED from +0.5% because the Acting CEO has now also carried the CFO, COO NZ and Company Secretary roles for more than eight months through a turnaround with no permanent appointment disclosed. The premium would revert to +0.5% on a permanent CEO appointment and to zero once that person has delivered a full year. Survival risk lives here, not in the cash flows; the scenarios differ only in operating trajectory and use the same rate.
wacc_rationale.charge_once_note: The scenario weights (35% bear) and the WACC premiums overlap in what they price. The deliberate split is: WACC = the risk that the equity is impaired (concentration, illiquidity, leadership, secular decline); scenario weights = how the operating business trades if it survives. A reader who thinks that double-charges can read the sensitivity row at 15.5%.

terminal_value_policy.rule: TV = max(0, min(Gordon, cap x FCF_FY2031)); cap 12x (structurally slow, mail-exposed micro-cap); end-of-year discounting; 5-year horizon because base/bull margins are flat by FY2030-31
terminal_value_policy.note: At a 17.5% WACC the Gordon multiple is only ~6.6x so the cap never binds. The bear case hits the ZERO FLOOR: terminal FCF is negative, meaning the business does not survive that path and the residual value is the remaining cash after five years of burn -- a finding, not a rounding detail.

base.label: Base -- reset base holds, margin recovers to 9% (IFRS-16) as cost-out completes
base.narrative: Axes: whether the ~NZ$31m post-customer-loss revenue base holds against continuing print-to-digital migration, and whether the SG&A cuts of FY2025-H1 FY2026 restore an IFRS-16 EBITDA margin near the 9-10% the smaller FY2017-18 business earned. Revenue slips ~4% in FY2027 (H2 FY2026 run-rate was below H1) then stabilises; no LWDW or nGAGE revenue is credited because none has been announced. nGAGE spend continues inside the margin path. The result is owner FCF of ~NZ$0.56m in FY2027 rising to ~NZ$1.23m by FY2031 -- roughly what the FY2017-18 business earned on NZ$20-23m of revenue.
base.fcf_assumption: Component build: IFRS-16 EBITDA margin 6.0% -> 9.0% (FY2026 actual ~4.3%; pre-reset 10.8-14.1%), less NZ$0.83m/yr lease cash, NZ$0.40m non-ROU D&A, 28% tax, NZ$0.30m maintenance capex (post-inserter guidance is minimal). Normalized FY2031 owner FCF NZ$1.23m replaces the June model's asserted NZ$2.0m base / NZ$2.24m terminal.
base.growth_rationale: FY2027 -3.8% (H2 FY2026 annualised is ~NZ$28.6m, H1-weighted seasonality lifts the year to ~NZ$30.2m), then -1%, +1%, +2%, +2% as digital/SaaS (Pitney Bowes clicks, existing council omni-channel conversion) offsets physical-mail erosion.

component_build.note: Owner FCF built per year from components on the FY2026 revenue base (~NZ$31.4m, aggregator figure, unverified). EBITDA margin is on the IFRS-16 (post-lease) basis the CSV reports; the full lease cash cost (~NZ$0.83m/yr principal + interest) is then charged as an operating cost, so lease liabilities are excluded from net cash (treatment B). Interest income is excluded because the cash pile is added back in the bridge. Tax 28% NZ statutory on positive EBIT, 0% on losses (no refund assumed). Working capital = -3% x change in revenue (decline releases, growth consumes).

bull.label: Bull -- LWDW water-entity billing wins + nGAGE scales + permanent CEO
bull.narrative: Axes: SDL wins billing-communications contracts from several of the 18 council-controlled water organisations (5 live from 1-Jul-2026, 13 more within 12 months) as they move to direct consumer billing; nGAGE grows beyond the two UK dental groups (58+ sites) into a material SaaS line; a permanent CEO is appointed; NZ mailhouse consolidation (a competitor exiting) adds volume. Revenue returns to growth from FY2028 and the IFRS-16 EBITDA margin recovers to ~12% -- still below the FY2023-24 peak. Terminal owner FCF ~NZ$2.45m is BELOW the June model's base case: even the bull no longer reaches the pre-reset run-rate.
bull.fcf_assumption: Margin 7.0% -> 12.0% on growing revenue; capex rises to NZ$0.40m with volume; working capital consumes 3% of the revenue increase.
bull.growth_rationale: Flat FY2027, then +5%, +7%, +6%, +5% -- requires three independent things (water-entity wins, nGAGE traction, leadership) to go right, hence the 20% weight.

component_build.note: Owner FCF built per year from components on the FY2026 revenue base (~NZ$31.4m, aggregator figure, unverified). EBITDA margin is on the IFRS-16 (post-lease) basis the CSV reports; the full lease cash cost (~NZ$0.83m/yr principal + interest) is then charged as an operating cost, so lease liabilities are excluded from net cash (treatment B). Interest income is excluded because the cash pile is added back in the bridge. Tax 28% NZ statutory on positive EBIT, 0% on losses (no refund assumed). Working capital = -3% x change in revenue (decline releases, growth consumes).

bear.label: Bear -- attrition continues, margin stuck near break-even, slow cash burn
bear.narrative: Axes: another top-5 customer or the Pitney Bowes channel shrinks; NZ Post pricing pushes remaining print volume to low-margin digital faster than costs can be cut; nGAGE keeps absorbing spend without revenue; the leadership gap persists. Revenue declines 8%%, 6%%, 4%%, 3%%, 2%% and the IFRS-16 EBITDA margin sits at 3-3.5%% -- i.e. the business earns roughly its lease cost and nothing more (FY2026 was ~4.3%%). Owner FCF turns negative from FY2028 and the terminal value floors at zero: the operating business is worth nothing and the cash pile shrinks by ~NZ$1.1m over five years (before whatever the Board keeps paying out as dividends, which merely moves cash to holders). This is the value-trap path and it is now partly evidenced by negative H1 FY2026 FCF.
bear.fcf_assumption: Margin 3.5% then 3.0%; capex NZ$0.25m; no tax on losses (no refund credited); working capital releases 3% of the revenue decline.
bear.growth_rationale: -8%, -6%, -4%, -3%, -2%: continued attrition among the concentrated top-5 plus faster mail erosion; new products fail to offset.

component_build.note: Owner FCF built per year from components on the FY2026 revenue base (~NZ$31.4m, aggregator figure, unverified). EBITDA margin is on the IFRS-16 (post-lease) basis the CSV reports; the full lease cash cost (~NZ$0.83m/yr principal + interest) is then charged as an operating cost, so lease liabilities are excluded from net cash (treatment B). Interest income is excluded because the cash pile is added back in the bridge. Tax 28% NZ statutory on positive EBIT, 0% on losses (no refund assumed). Working capital = -3% x change in revenue (decline releases, growth consumes).

bear.floor_flag: Terminal value hit the zero floor: FY2031 owner FCF is negative (NZ$-0.32m). Intrinsic value in this scenario is essentially net cash less five years of burn.

valuation._note: Mirror of scenarios.* for consumers that read valuation.{scenario}.intrinsic_value (sanity_check.py, dcf_fields.py). scenarios.* is the full record.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Prior 50/25/25. Bear raised to 35%: a full year at the depressed run-rate with H2 below H1, negative H1 FY2026 FCF, break-even underlying earnings and an eight-month leadership vacuum make the slow-burn path the best-evidenced alternative to the base. Bull cut to 20%: it needs water-entity wins, nGAGE traction and a permanent CEO to coincide, and none of the three has been announced. Base 45%: the reset base holding with margin recovery is still the single most likely path -- guidance was met, cost-out is done, capex is behind the company and the Board is still returning cash.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC-zero market: share-based payment expense NZ$21k FY2025 / NZ$24k FY2024 (FY2025 AR line 1423) is immaterial, so house and street bases coincide and the band collapses; band_position is null by design.

entry_price.method: Price at which buying today, collecting the projected owner FCF and exiting at FY2031 earns a 15% IRR: (sum FCF_t/1.15^t + TV@15%/1.15^5 + net cash) / shares, with TV rebuilt at the hurdle rate as max(0, min(FCF_5 x (1+g)/(0.15-g), 12 x FCF_5)) per the 2026-09-01 spec. Replaces the June method (terminal equity value discounted at 15% alone).
entry_price.important: The 15% house hurdle is BELOW this model's 17.5% WACC, so the hurdle entry price sits ABOVE intrinsic value in every scenario -- a 15% return is a lower bar than the rate the model says this equity needs. The operative buy-below price is therefore the weighted intrinsic value (NZ$0.861), not the weighted entry price; the entry figures are reported for cross-ticker comparability and equal the 15% row of required_return_table.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (min(Gordon@r, 12x), floored at 0). The 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price; the 17.5% row equals scenarios.base.intrinsic_value.
required_return_table.price_implied_return: On the base path, NZ$0.625 implies an IRR of 48.7% (bisection on the same closed form, TV rebuilt at that rate); on the weighted path 38.7%.

sensitivity.note: Base-case intrinsic value per share across WACC (rows) and terminal growth (columns); component-built FCF path held; TV = max(0, min(Gordon, 12x)); net cash NZ$7.17m, 14.43m shares.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fix_applied: Rebuilt on the confirmed reset base rather than adjusting a passing model: base normalized FCF cut ~45%, net cash rolled forward, WACC +0.5%, bear weight 25% -> 35%. | Agent diagnosis: No peak extrapolation: the base path starts at NZ$0.56m owner FCF (below the FY2026 underlying ~zero only by the margin recovery assumed) and matures at NZ$1.23m, under the pre-reset owner-FCF median of NZ$1.95m and under what the FY2017-18 business earned. Net cash is ~58% of the weighted IV; the operating business is valued at ~NZ$0.36/share weighted. The June model's larger gap to price was mostly an asserted NZ$2.0m FCF that FY2026 has since contradicted. | Framing: Deep-value / asset-backed, not a multi-bagger: ~NZ$0.50 of the NZ$0.625 price is estimated net cash (post the 4.0c dividend), the market pays ~NZ$0.13/share for a business guided to a small profit, and the weighted model says that business is worth ~NZ$0.36/share if it stabilises. The risk is a value trap in which the cash funds dividends, buybacks and a slow operating burn while the asset backing erodes (bear IV NZ$0.454, 27% below the price). Position sizing must reflect NZX micro-cap illiquidity; the catalyst that would move the base case is a disclosed water-entity contract or an nGAGE site count in the unparsed FY2026 annual report. | Note: scripts/sanity_check.py finds no DB-side P/E or P/B because metrics_normalized carries NULL units for SDL.NZ (CSV is populated); its historical table is price-only until units are backfilled.
